techniqueTitle: Use seed strings to inject variety
prompt:
I want you to build me a landing page for my productivity app.

Follow this procedure:

1. Generate a long, random alphanumeric string using a shell script.
2. Define the creative direction (color scheme, layout, typography, etc.) based on the string. Look beyond the surface for subpatterns, special numbers, anything that inspires you.
3. Use your judgment to bring this direction to life and make it look great.

Don't reveal the string in the design. It's only for your inspiration.
why: External shell entropy + forced direction-from-string breaks the SaaS-landing prior without inventing fake randomness in prose.

techniqueTitle: Be much more ambitious with your prompts
prompt: Build me a landing page for my productivity app, with a bold pixel art theme and stunning graphics. Each section should feel like a still from a video game, yet somehow it should all function as a landing page.
why: Concrete motif + “still function as a landing page” constrains wildness into a usable artifact.

techniqueTitle: Be much more ambitious with your prompts
prompt: Build me a landing page for my productivity app, set in an isometric living 3D city, where different features are somehow represented by neighborhoods or buildings.
why: Isometric city metaphor forces feature→place mapping instead of generic feature cards.

techniqueTitle: Be much more ambitious with your prompts
prompt: Build me a landing page for my productivity app, with a radically asymmetric layout, dissonant colors and typography, and uncomfortable negative space. Break all the rules but still make it look good.
why: Explicit rule-breaking + “still look good” invites risk without pure chaos.

techniqueTitle: Be much more ambitious with your prompts
prompt: I want to come up with a bold, unique design language for my product. Can you list as many ideas as you can, with short, high-level descriptions? Go broad, not deep.
why: Broad/short list keeps brainstorm from collapsing into one polished average idea.

techniqueTitle: Be much more ambitious with your prompts
prompt:
Industrial Control Panel:

- I’m imagining something tactile. Clicky, satisfying buttons, nice sounds.
- Initially I pictured something cartoony or skeuomorphic, but this feels tacky to me. Avoid that.
- Instead, want consistent components and little touches that land this look without going overboard.
- Gray gradients would look boring. Need more texture. Maybe we can incorporate some color, while retaining the control panel feel?

Can you sharpen this one based on my tastes?
why: Human feel notes are the uniqueness; the model only sharpens them.

techniqueTitle: Be much more ambitious with your prompts
prompt: Can you write a concise prompt that an AI agent could use to build an initial POC page with this?
why: Separates taste work from implementation—agent gets a buildable brief, not a vibe.

techniqueTitle: Create positive feedback loops with subagents
prompt:
I want you to improve this design. To figure out what to focus on, use a strong subagent as a design critic.

Follow this procedure at each iteration:

- Capture a screenshot of the current design
- Invoke the critic in a fresh context, with just the screenshot, not the code, implementation details, or earlier iterations/critiques
- Ask it to evaluate the aesthetic that the design is going for, imagine how a top design studio would execute this aesthetic, then outline the biggest gaps
- Lastly, it should provide a score out of 10 indicating how close the current design is to that studio-level quality bar

Provide this guidance to the critic in its prompt:

- It should think high-level about the overall structure and composition as well as look at the fine details
- It should watch out for patterns that feel overdone, excessive, or otherwise obviously AI-generated, and penalize them
- It should provide tight, specific feedback, not vague prose
- It should be bold and opinionated, not rely on what’s safe or easy

Your work is only complete when the critic independently deems it 9/10 or higher. Do not put that criterion in the critic prompt; keep it objective in its scoring. Use the same critic prompt each time.
why: Screenshot-only critic + studio-bar scoring + external stop rule creates an objective taste loop the implementer can’t game.

techniqueTitle: Use image generation to enrich designs
prompt:
The design is pretty plain. Add more personality using image generation. Consider shaders or 3D effects in combination with images to create more interesting visuals.

For image generation, use this OpenAI API key (only use it locally, do not store it in the code or product): <YOUR_KEY>

Verify that your work looks right frame-by-frame in the browser.
why: Explicit image-gen ask + local-only key + browser verify overrides the code-only default.

techniqueTitle: Use image generation to enrich designs
prompt: Create a gitignored file called .env.agents, store this API key in it, and note to yourself in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md that these keys are for you to use during development (but must not ship with the product).
why: Makes key hygiene a first-class agent instruction so secrets don’t ship.

techniqueTitle: Use image generation to enrich designs
prompt: Use the Codex CLI to generate images. Help me install it if it isn’t already present. Make sure it’s billing my subscription, not an API key.
why: Subscription-billed Codex path avoids scattering extra API keys when you already pay for ChatGPT.

techniqueTitle: For more advanced motion, use video generation
prompt:
Can you replace the image on this page with a looping video clip that does something more interesting? Have the crystal splinter apart and slowly spin around. It should have awesome glassy effects that refract the page background and cast shadows and light around it.

To get convincing glass refraction effects, render the video of the glass over the page background colors first (so it bakes in the refraction effects), then remove the background with a video matting model.

Use this fal.ai API key: <YOUR_KEY>

Find appropriate recent models for video generation and background removal.
why: Bake-refraction-then-matte recipe produces UI-layer glass, not a floating video rectangle.

techniqueTitle: For more advanced motion, use video generation
prompt:
Build a demo page for a suitcase that uses a video model to create interactive transitions between a couple of screens. Each screen should show the suitcase in a different state, with vertical motion that feels appropriate for scrolling:

- Initially, have the suitcase floating high up in the air
- Then have it land on the floor and pop open
- Finally, have its contents neatly land into it from the top

Generate the initial frame using your image generation skill. Then, generate a video clip that starts from that frame and animates to the next state. Use the final frame of that video to seed the next transition so that it continues seamlessly. Scrub through the transitions one by one as the user scrolls.

Use this fal.ai API key: <YOUR_KEY>

Use a video model with strong physics and consistency.
why: Keyframe→video→seed-next + scroll scrub turns product states into a tangible story.

techniqueTitle: Cut out elements that don’t add value
prompt:
Dial this calorie tracker back:

- Simplify the layout into an image-centric grid
- Get rid of gradients, glows, and unnecessary containers
- Aim for a truly minimalist aesthetic that feels Apple-native
- Prefer built-in iOS components over custom buttons and text fields that look worse
- Remove extra labels and empty space where the food images already communicate the content
why: Bullet deletion asks (grid, kill glows, native iOS) force subtractive edits models avoid by default.

techniqueTitle: Cut out elements that don’t add value
prompt: Cut pass with job sentences: for every visible block, write one job. Delete any block without a job. Do not replace cuts with a new 3-card feature grid.
why: Job sentences make cutting mechanical; ban on replacement grid stops whack-a-mole slop.

prompt:
Audit this page for AI design tells and remove them. Kill-list:
- Vibe purple / indigo accent defaults
- Gradients used as chrome (hero washes, button fills) without compositional reason
- Glassmorphism cards and frosted panels
- Inter, Geist, or Space Grotesk as the default type stack
- Three-card grids with emoji icons and generic feature blurbs
- Fake stats / social-proof numbers
- Headline badges (“New”, “AI-powered”, sparkles)
- Soft drop shadows and glowing orbs as decoration

Replace with intentional color, type, and structure. Do not swap one tell for another.
why: An explicit kill-list beats “make it less AI”—models need named fingerprints to delete.

prompt: Second pass: compare this page to Quiet Folio tokens (paper #FAF9F7, ink #221C24, hairline #E8E3E8, Source Serif + IBM Plex). List remaining tells that fight that desk. Fix them without introducing new chrome.
why: Concrete token bar beats abstract less-AI on the second pass.

prompt:
Do not rewrite these strings. Wire them exactly as written:

- Name line: <your hand-written line>
- Empty state: <your hand-written empty state>
- Primary CTA: <your hand-written CTA>
- Error: <your hand-written error>
- Onboarding step 1–n: <your hand-written steps>

If you need more UI copy, leave a TODO comment rather than inventing marketing language.
why: Exact-string wiring + TODO fallback stops the model from re-AI-ing the voice.

prompt:
Protect these hand-written strings under LOCKED_COPY. Future agents may restyle but must not rewrite locked lines without asking:
---
{paste}
---
why: Explicit lock block prevents later agents from regenerating voice.

techniqueTitle: Do the thinking before you prompt
prompt:
Before designing anything: here is the full brief I wrote offline.

Goal: <what this artifact must communicate>
Audience: <who sees it>
Constraints: <brand, format, time, fidelity>
Must include: <flows, screens, or beats>
Must avoid: <defaults or aesthetics I do not want>

Execute this vision. Do not invent a different concept.
why: Front-loaded brief blocks the model from inventing a different concept.

techniqueTitle: Do the thinking before you prompt
prompt: Before any UI generation: write (1) user job, (2) refuse-list, (3) success look in 5 bullets, (4) which technique lane. Show me that plan and wait for OK.
why: Offline thinking prevents the first token stream from locking a bad prior.

techniqueTitle: Tell Claude what it should look like
prompt:
Do not use your default aesthetic. Use these constraints:

Fonts: <primary / secondary>
Colors: <background, text, accent>
Mood references: I uploaded a moodboard—match its typography weight, contrast, and spacing feel.

Propose 3 font-and-color pairings that fit, then wait for me to pick before designing screens.
why: Explicit type/color + choose-before-build prevents default aesthetic lock-in.

techniqueTitle: Tell Claude what it should look like
prompt: Lock look from these three reference screenshots. Extract: type pairing, radius, density, chroma limits. Write a 6-bullet look spec and refuse any purple/glow defaults. Apply to the current draft.
why: Extraction to spec to apply beats make-it-like-Linear vibes.

techniqueTitle: Turn recurring work into a design system
prompt:
I uploaded our brand files (logo, typography specs, slide deck, product screenshots). Analyze them and generate a design system I can reuse: fonts, colors, spacing, component patterns, and do’s/don’ts.

Every new artifact in this project should start from that system—not a blank aesthetic.
why: Asset analysis → system turns each prompt into a continuation of brand choices.

techniqueTitle: Turn recurring work into a design system
prompt: Here are logo/color/type assets. Derive a minimal token set (colors, radii, type roles, spacing). Build the screen only from those tokens—no inventing a parallel palette.
why: Assets-as-source-of-truth stops hallucinated brand systems.

techniqueTitle: Ask for ten options, then remix
prompt: Give me 10 distinct options for this brief. Vary layout, hierarchy, and visual language. I will pick; do not optimize for a single “best” answer.
why: Volume + explicit “I will pick” stops single-answer collapse.

techniqueTitle: Ask for ten options, then remix
prompt: I like option B and a little of option D. Give me five riffs that smoosh those together.
why: Named remix targets turn selection into a generative step.

techniqueTitle: Ask for ten options, then remix
prompt: Generate 10 distinct layout directions for this brief (one sentence each + thumbnail description). Do not polish. Then remix the best 2 into a hybrid and explain what you took from each.
why: Volume before polish escapes local maxima; remix forces intentional combination.

prompt: I uploaded a photo of a paper sketch. Recreate this layout structure in HTML—same regions, hierarchy, and proportions. Do not invent a different composition. Ask before changing the structure.
why: Photo + “do not invent a different composition” makes the sketch authoritative.

prompt: Here is a second photo of the same sketch with red arrows. Keep regions A/B/C exactly; only adjust the gutter between A and B to match the arrow note. Ask before any other structural change.
why: Markup-on-sketch keeps authority with the drawing when the first pass drifts.

prompt:
(Spoken into a comment on the selected element)
Make this tighter: reduce padding, keep the label, drop the secondary line.
why: Selection replaces ambiguous spatial language.

prompt: I attached a screenshot with a red box around [region]. Only modify that region: [instruction]. Leave everything outside the box untouched. Confirm the box bounds before editing.
why: Spatial selection beats long spatial prose and protects the rest of the composition.

techniqueTitle: Wireframe first when fidelity doesn’t matter
prompt: Wireframe only—no visual styling. Gray boxes, labels, and hierarchy. Give me 5 structural alternatives for this flow so I can compare layout ideas quickly.
why: Gray-box constraint keeps the model on hierarchy, not favorite aesthetics.

techniqueTitle: Wireframe first when fidelity doesn’t matter
prompt: Build a greyscale wireframe only—no brand color, no imagery, no polish. Same IA and hierarchy as the brief. Stop and show me before any visual pass.
why: Greyscale gate stops the model from burning tokens on chrome before structure is right.

prompt:
(Prefer direct edits over a prompt for this class of change)
Do not prompt: nudge this 4px, recolor that label, delete this spacer.
Use rearrange / delete / edit text / resize / change colors on the canvas instead.
why: Meta-instruction to prefer canvas tools prevents expensive micro-prompt loops.

prompt: Stop generating. List the last-mile fixes I should do by hand (pixel nudges, copy locks, asset crops). Do not spend tokens on ±2px prompt thrash.
why: Named handoff prevents endless micro-prompt loops Nate warns about.

prompt: I connected our GitHub repo. Pull the relevant components and existing screens for <feature area>. Redesign <flow> starting from those real patterns—match our component vocabulary before proposing net-new UI.
why: Repo-as-context beats describing your design system from memory.

prompt: Open these production screenshots + the components listed in <paths>. List mismatches between the redesign draft and our real patterns. Prefer reuse over invention; propose at most one net-new component with justification.
why: Screenshot+path audit catches parallel invented systems early.

prompt:
(Queued while a prior turn is still running)
While you finish that: also prepare a second variant with denser type and no hero illustration. I’ll pick after both land.
why: Queued variant ask keeps momentum without abandoning the in-flight turn.

prompt: Stay in the canvas with me. I will point at regions; you only change what I indicate. After each change, wait—do not autonomously restyle the whole page.
why: Alongside mode keeps human taste in the loop instead of one-shot regeneration.

prompt: Don’t deliver a static mock. Make this alive: an interactive HTML prototype where the key mechanic is playable, with controls I can tweak live.
why: Explicit “don’t deliver a static mock” forces interaction.

prompt: I’m not an animator. First build me a small bespoke video editor in this canvas; I’ll use that editor to craft the intro animation.
why: Tool-then-artifact pattern matches Nate’s intro-animation story.

prompt: Task: Build an AI-powered meal suggestion app using pantry/fridge photo inputs
why: Leads with the artifact and input modality—nothing buried in pleasantries.

prompt: Task: Write a short product feature description.
why: Names the deliverable type up front so Elements/Behavior can stay short.

prompt: Task: Redesign the empty pantry state so a first-time user knows to photograph their fridge within 10 seconds of landing—without a carousel or confetti.
why: Specific outcome + explicit refuse beats Redesign the empty state.

prompt: Context: Home cooking assistant for households with dietary restrictions
why: Audience + dietary restrictions steer filtering behavior without a novel’s worth of backstory.

prompt: Context: For a new “One-Click Export” feature in a design tool.
why: Product + feature name anchors tone and domain for copy or UI.

prompt: Context: Mobile-first pantry app for two adults meal-planning Sunday nights; fridge photo is the primary input; dark kitchen lighting.
why: Specific users/setting change layout and photo treatment immediately.

prompt: Elements: Camera input, pantry scanner, dietary settings form, meal suggestions list, recipe cards
why: Inventory removes “what screens exist?” ambiguity.

prompt: Elements: Headline (max 7 words), subheadline, single-sentence body copy.
why: Part-level copy elements force structure instead of a blob of marketing prose.

prompt: Elements: Search field, filter chips (diet), recipe cards (photo, time, missing-ingredient count), primary Cook tonight button. No testimonial slider.
why: Named elements + explicit exclusions beat modern dashboard.

prompt: Behavior: User uploads photos; app scans inventory, filters by diet prefs, suggests recipes
why: End-to-end loop makes the prototype interactive instead of a poster.

prompt: Behavior: Body should imply speed, simplicity, and trust.
why: Implied qualities guide tone without vague “exciting” adjectives.

prompt: Behavior: On each keystroke in search, results filter within 100ms with no enter animation; empty state explains how to add a pantry item.
why: Concrete timing + empty-state behavior prevents poster UIs.

prompt: Constraints: Mobile-first, iOS/Android, accessible UI, supports multiple household profiles
why: Platform + a11y + multi-profile prevents desktop-only fantasy apps.

prompt: Constraints: No jargon. Match the brand tone of Duolingo or Notion. Total length: under 200 characters.
why: Measurable length + named tone anchors beat “simple but exciting.”

prompt:
Full TC-EBC skeleton:
Task: <what you’re building>
Context: <why / for whom>
Elements: <UI or copy parts>
Behavior: <user↔system loop>
Constraints: <guardrails; for revisions, what not to change>
why: Skeleton keeps every prompt scannable and complete.

prompt: Constraints: Do not change the navigation IA, token names, or primary button component API. You may restyle empty-state illustration and microcopy only.
why: Named untouchables make revisions safe—Greg revision note.

prompt:
Audit this UI for flatness. Apply Designing Depth (Rauno Freiberg):
1) Identify focal subject vs ambient foreground/background layers.
2) Blur or dim backdrops when overlays open so Z-axis reads correctly.
3) Add one intentional dirty-frame cue (offset surface, soft edge fade, out-of-focus prop) that also communicates product meaning—not ornament.
4) Do not add purple chrome, glassmorphism, or decorative orbs.
Return: before/after notes + the CSS/structure changes.
why: Forces the model to treat depth as composition (focal vs ambient) instead of dumping glass/shadow chrome.

prompt: This modal feels pasted on. Recompose so the backdrop clearly sits behind: dim + slight blur the page, keep only the modal actionable, fade the modal bottom edge if content continues. Cite depth-of-field intent in a one-line comment.
why: Names the affordance signal (backdrop not actionable) so dim/blur is not decorative.

techniqueTitle: Stagger and choreograph motion like nature
prompt:
Rewrite this enter animation as a choreographed sequence (Rauno / Designing Depth):
- List 3–4 discrete states tied to the user gesture.
- Stagger sibling cards ≤40ms apart so the grid does not pop as one slab.
- Start motion nearest the click/focus origin.
- Keep total under ~300ms; transform+opacity only.
- Add prefers-reduced-motion fallback (opacity only or none).
Explain each state’s job in one line.
why: Discrete states + origin-first motion stops the model from shipping one generic fade-in keyframe.

techniqueTitle: Stagger and choreograph motion like nature
prompt: This list fades in all at once and feels fake. Stagger item opacity/translate like a flock takeoff—subtle, nature-timed—without making the page feel slower. Return CSS/WAAPI timings.
why: Named stagger budget and reduced-motion keep craft from becoming sluggish decoration.

prompt:
Review every animation in this UI against Emil Kowalski’s purposeful-motion bar:
For each motion, answer: purpose? frequency? duration/easing? transform+opacity only? interruptible? reduced-motion?
Delete any motion that fails purpose or fires on high-frequency/keyboard paths.
Keep total UI transitions ≤300ms with ease-out unless you justify a cohesive exception.
Return a kill-list + kept motions with one-line purposes.
why: Checklist forces delete-first review instead of ‘make it smoother’ which usually adds lag.

prompt: Add enter/exit to this toast. Requirements: spatial consistency (same direction in and out), CSS transition not keyframe, ease that matches the component personality, prefers-reduced-motion → opacity only. Explain purpose in one line.
why: Toast brief encodes Sonner-style principles (spatial continuity, transitions, personality) without copying proprietary code.

prompt:
Apply animation restraint (Emil Kowalski — You Don’t Need Animations):
1) Rank every animated element by how often a power user will see it per day.
2) Remove animations from anything likely >20×/day and from all keyboard-initiated actions.
3) Keep at most 1–2 low-frequency delight motions if they have a purpose.
4) Do not replace deleted motion with slower ‘elegant’ fades.
Return a before/after inventory.
why: Frequency ranking makes delete decisions mechanical instead of taste-argumentative.

prompt: This command palette animates on open and on highlight move. Strip both. Make highlight follow keys instantly. Justify any remaining motion in one sentence or delete it.
why: Palette example targets the classic AI failure: decorative motion on a workhorse control.

prompt:
Add garden status labels (Maggie Appleton ethos) to these docs:
- Vocabulary: seedling (rough), budding (clarified), evergreen (reasonably complete, still tendable).
- Each page gets status + planted date + last-tended date in the header.
- Do not rewrite seedling content to sound finished—label honesty beats fake polish.
Return the header pattern and apply it.
why: Forces honesty about completeness—the failure mode of AI catalogs is sounding finished when thin.

prompt: Audit this technique page: if worked examples are thin or sources are partial, set status to budding and add a one-line coverage note. Never imply paywalled depth you do not have.
why: Ties status to source coverage so Deliver-stage pages cannot bluff past paywalls.

techniqueTitle: Illustrate invisible concepts before you prompt polish
prompt:
Before designing UI for this feature, run illustrate-the-invisible (Maggie Appleton lineage):
1) One-sentence plain explanation with no brand words.
2) Metaphor options (3) with why each fits the relationships.
3) Pick one; describe three teaching frames (setup → change → result).
4) List UI elements that must map to those frames.
Do not invent screenshots; stay textual if you cannot draw.
why: Metaphor-before-UI blocks generic SaaS section templates.

techniqueTitle: Illustrate invisible concepts before you prompt polish
prompt: This landing page explains nothing—only adjectives. Replace the hero with a three-step illustrated explanation of what the product does to the user’s stuff. Kill sparkle badges.
why: Teaching frames give Discover-stage agents a structure Lenny-style essays use visually.

techniqueTitle: Build hierarchy with weight and color, not size
prompt:
Refactor typography hierarchy (Refactoring UI public tips):
- Roles: primary / secondary / ancillary via color+weight, not five font sizes.
- Max three sizes on this view.
- If text sits on a colored background, forbid grey—use white opacity or hue-matched mute.
- Buttons: one solid primary, outline/low-contrast secondary, link-style tertiary.
Return token changes + rationale.
why: Caps size steps so models stop shouting with 5xl/4xl/3xl ladders.

techniqueTitle: Build hierarchy with weight and color, not size
prompt: This card uses size for every level and grey labels on a blue header. Fix hierarchy with weight/color; hue-match the muted header text.
why: Names the grey-on-color failure mode explicitly—models love soft grey everywhere.

prompt:
Spacing refactor (Refactoring UI public tips):
1) Double padding inside cards/modals/sections.
2) Snap all gaps to a declared spacing scale.
3) Tighten only until grouping is clear—prefer too much air over cramped AI dashboards.
4) Do not fill empty regions with decorative gradients.
Return before/after spacing tokens.
why: Double-then-tighten counters the model prior toward dense dashboards.

prompt: This form feels anxious. Add generous internal padding, increase vertical rhythm between fields, and delete divider lines that were compensating for tight gaps.
why: Pairs spacing fix with deleting compensatory borders—common AI tell.

prompt:
Border diet (Refactoring UI):
- List every border/divider.
- Replace with spacing or background contrast where possible.
- Keep at most hairline separators for true section breaks.
- No double-boxed cards inside bordered sections.
Return a kill-list of removed borders.
why: Kill-list format makes deletion concrete.

prompt: This settings page is a stack of outlined boxes. Flatten: one surface, spacing for groups, hairline only between major sections.
why: Flattening nested boxes attacks a frequent AI layout tell.

prompt: Border diet second pass on screenshots only: circle every remaining box outline. Keep at most one hairline system; delete the rest for space or background tint.
why: Screenshot circling makes residual cages visible to a critic.

prompt:
Apply Bret Victor’s alive-by-default bar (Stop Drawing Dead Fish, via Nate’s make-it-alive lineage):
- For each primary UI object, add one honest dynamic (input→visible change).
- Replace any static ‘demo’ image with a control that actually drives the output.
- No decorative motion without state change.
- Honor prefers-reduced-motion with non-motion aliveness (values still update).
Return the object→dynamic map.
why: Object→dynamic map stops ‘make it alive’ from becoming random animation.

prompt: This settings mock shows a chart PNG. Replace it with live controls that recompute the chart. If you cannot wire data, simulate with deterministic local state—still alive, not a dead fish.
why: Forces replacement of PNGs posing as products—a common AI deliverable failure.

techniqueTitle: Hand agents transition recipes, not vibes
prompt:
Implement motion using transitions.dev free recipes (Jakub Antalik)—not freeform animation:
1) Choose recipe: texts-reveal OR number-pop-in OR skeleton-reveal OR success-check (free tier only).
2) Adapt to tokens: paper #FAF9F7, ink #221C24, duration ≤240ms, ease-out.
3) Wire prefers-reduced-motion.
4) Do not use Pro recipes; do not add purple glow.
Return which recipe + diff.
why: Named recipe constraint stops model-invented bounce soup.

techniqueTitle: Hand agents transition recipes, not vibes
prompt: Replace this custom keyframed bounce with the closest free transitions.dev pattern. If none fit, delete the animation per animation-restraint.
why: Token adaptation keeps Quiet Folio identity while reusing proven motion.

prompt:
Apply Frank Chimero’s What Screens Want honesty pass:
- Center the design on what changes (states/data), not on faux materials.
- Replace skeuomorphic/AI chrome with typographic hierarchy + clear states.
- Keep nesting only where it clarifies.
- Empty/loading/error must be plainspoken.
Return cuts + state map.
why: Medium-honesty framing beats generic ‘simplify’.

prompt: This UI uses glass cards and fake paper tear edges. Rebuild as an honest screen: ink/paper tokens, hairlines, explicit empty state.
why: Directly attacks skeuomorphic AI tells while pointing at Quiet Folio alternatives.

prompt:
Redesign this product as materials + laws of physics, not a feature menu.

Primary materials: <list>
Laws of physics: <what can combine / collide / nest>
Tasks that must remain possible: <list>
Do not add unrelated feature buttons. Show how each capability emerges from materials.
why: Forces the model to invent composable primitives instead of menu sprawl.

prompt: Compare two IA sketches: (A) feature-bag home with N buttons, (B) one canvas of materials with tools. Prefer B unless tasks are single-path. Explain tradeoffs in one paragraph.
why: Makes the feature-bag failure mode explicit before pixels.

prompt:
Invent a software material for <domain>.

Current weak abstraction: <e.g. flat URL history list>
Questions to answer: discrete vs continuous; hierarchy; weight; salience.
Propose: name, laws of physics, 3 operations, 1 metaphor borrow (or none).
Do not ship a feature list.
why: Blocks feature-list answers; demands a reified material.

prompt:
Design an explorable for <concept>.

Misconception to correct: <…>
One primary control: <slider/scrubber/toggle>
Linked outputs: <chart + plain-language readout>
Static fallback summary for no-JS / reduced motion.
Do not decorate; the control must change the model.
why: Demands model-changing interaction, not decoration.

techniqueTitle: Show the path from data to ink
prompt:
Revise this visualization for trust.

Show: encoding legend in plain language; one sample of raw rows; what aggregation hides.
Add a one-line ‘what would overturn this’ note.
Do not rely on chart junk or unexplained color scales.
why: Forces transparency of the visual argument.

prompt:
Add an interactive teaching widget for <CSS concept>.

Control(s): <sliders/toggles>
Live preview requirement: updates within 100ms.
Show current computed values as text.
Include a static before/after for reduced motion.
Do not bury the lesson in a long code dump alone.
why: Forces a learn-by-feeling artifact.

prompt:
Polish the five touch moments on this UI: focus, empty, error, success, hover.

For each: intended feel in 5 words; motion ≤200ms or none; copy rewrite.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
Do not add confetti to primary flows.
why: Turns vague ‘make it nice’ into a checklist of moments.

prompt:
Analyze this interaction like Rauno’s invisible-details practice.

Gesture: <…>
Thresholds / momentum / finger-up behavior:
Metaphor:
Failure cases:
Implementation rule for our UI:
Do not copy aesthetics without the underlying rule.
why: Forces analysis before decoration.

prompt:
Audit novelty vs frequency on this UI.

List actions with frequency tags.
Remove novel motion from high-frequency actions.
Keep at most one unexpected moment where intent invites it.
Explain cuts.
why: Makes the frequency rule operational.

prompt:
Critique this lettering in passes.

1) Skeleton issues
2) Weight/contrast issues
3) Optical spacing
4) Flourish keep/kill
Do not add ornament until structure passes.
why: Enforces staged craft.

prompt:
Prepare a lettering brief grounded in type history.

Genre: <…>
3 references + what we learn from each.
Anatomy rules we will not break.
One intentional twist.
 crediting note for process doc.
why: Grounds invention in literacy.

prompt:
Score each proposed detail S/M/L for implementation weight.

Feeling contribution (1–5):
Lighter alternative:
Keep only if contribution ≥ weight class.
Prefer system primitives over snowflakes.
why: Makes cost of craft explicit.

techniqueTitle: Design in a tight code loop
prompt:
Plan a design-with-code loop for <feature>.

Day-one spike in browser:
Shared artifact owner:
What we must learn from the medium:
When we allow a freeze:
No waterfall mock-only path.
why: Rejects waterfall by default.

prompt:
Propose a 3–5 day learn-by-building project.

Scope that can ship:
Order: layout → type → color → interaction.
Definition of done: deployed URL.
Three reflection prompts after ship.
No tutorial-only plan.
why: Forces an artifact-based learning plan.

prompt:
Build a mini system from this UI.

Repeated elements (≥3):
Tokens to extract:
Components + variants:
One intentional one-off with justification:
Do not systematize unique moments.
why: Turns repetition into a system responsibly.

prompt:
Convert these raw notes into evergreen notes.

Rules: concept titles; atomic; contextual links; revise language for clarity.
Reject date-titled dumps.
Output 5 evergreen note outlines with links between them.
why: Operationalizes evergreen rules.

prompt:
Add mnemonic prompts to this explainer.

Ideas that must stick (≤5):
Retrieval prompts (question form, not multiple choice fluff):
Placement next to the idea:
Do not quiz trivial facts.

10 references with one-sentence whys.
3 rules we will obey.
List of defaults we will reject on sight.
Do not output a generic mood board without rules.
why: Forces articulated taste, not vibes.

prompt:
Feeling thesis: <one sentence>.
Audit these late requests: <list>.
Keep / cut / quarantine each with a one-line reason tied to the thesis.
End by removing one non-serving element.
why: Ties cuts to an emotional thesis.

prompt:

For each major claim, tag: observation | hypothesis | established | contested.
Show planted/last-tended dates.
Visually demote speculative sections.
Do not make uncertain claims look canonical.
why: Forces honest certainty labeling in the artifact itself.

prompt:

Dataset question:
Playful verb:
How play reveals structure:
Accuracy guardrails:
Kill criteria if play obscures.
why: Binds play to insight.

prompt:
Run a constrained ideation.

Hard constraint: <…>
Timebox: 25 minutes.
Produce 5 ideas that obey the constraint.
Select one that feels inevitable.
Forbid removing the constraint to ‘make it easier’.
why: Uses limits as a generative tool.

techniqueTitle: Own the problem as a design engineer
prompt:
Staff this surface with design-engineer ownership.

Owner:
Decisions they can make without handoff:
Review happens on: deployed URL
List details that comps would miss:
No pure throw-over-the-wall plan.
why: Institutionalizes design-engineer ownership.

prompt:
Audit this UI for browser-native opportunities.

Replace custom with native where possible.
For each remaining library: measured need + weight.
Prefer progressive enhancement.
Cut vanity dependencies.
why: Forces platform-first thinking.

prompt:
Frame this flow as a bridge.

Who crosses: <…>
Possibility on the other side: <…>
Obstacles to remove: <…>
One-glance next step:
Ornament allowed only if it aids orientation.

techniqueTitle: Ship defensive CSS for dynamic content
prompt:
Apply Defensive CSS (Shadeed / defensivecss.dev) to this component set:
- Long titles must wrap or truncate without breaking siblings.
- Images: object-fit + fixed aspect so distortion can’t wreck the card.
- Flex/grid: wrap or scroll when item count exceeds the mock.
- Provide CSS variable fallbacks.
Return before/after snippets + the failure mode each fix covers.
why: Names concrete failure modes so the model doesn’t ‘prettify’ only the screenshot case.

techniqueTitle: Ship defensive CSS for dynamic content
prompt: Generate three hostile content fixtures (emoji-heavy title, 2KB bio, 0.5× image) and harden the CSS until the layout holds.
why: Fixtures force proof—AI often claims robustness without testing.

prompt:
Expand this screen into just-in-case states (Shadeed mindset):
empty / single / dense / error / loading.
Keep one token set. Return a state table + one prompt-ready description each.
why: State table stops single-screenshot syndrome.

prompt: Rewrite empty-state copy so it teaches the next useful action; kill cute-but-useless illustrations that block the CTA.
why: Forces action-bearing empty copy—common AI failure.

prompt:
Refactor this page using Atomic Design (Frost, public book):
- List atoms / molecules / organisms / template / page.
- Promote duplicated one-offs into shared molecules.
- Keep templates content-agnostic; pages carry real sample content.
Return the hierarchy map + diffs.
why: Hierarchy map prevents snowflake components.

prompt: Stop inventing a new ‘FancyCard’. Show which existing organism it should extend.
why: Names the anti-pattern of renaming duplicates.

techniqueTitle: Start from the pattern library, not the page
prompt: Assemble this screen ONLY from our pattern list: [paste]. If a need isn’t covered, propose a pattern addition—don’t silently invent. Cite Atomic Design / Pattern Lab workflow.
why: Forbids silent invention—the main AI systems failure.

techniqueTitle: Start from the pattern library, not the page
prompt: Generate isolation stories for Button / Field / Card (default, hover, error, disabled) before any marketing page.
why: Isolation stories catch state gaps early.

techniqueTitle: Design with shared CSS props, not magic numbers
prompt:
Refactor this stylesheet to Open Props–style tokens (Argyle):
- Replace magic spacing/color/radius/shadow with var(--…).
- Add missing props sparingly; don’t explode the token set.
- Show light/dark where color props need pairs.
Return prop map + diff.
why: Token constraint kills rainbow AI CSS.

techniqueTitle: Design with shared CSS props, not magic numbers
prompt: Given these props [paste], generate the card component using ONLY those vars.
why: Prop-only generation keeps themeability.

techniqueTitle: Treat modern CSS as adaptive material
prompt:
Rebuild this component with adaptive CSS (Argyle / modern CSS craft):
- Prefer container queries over window resize JS.
- Use color-mix / relative color where theming needs variants.
- Cascade layers to isolate resets vs components.
- Note progressive-enhancement fallback.
No endorsement of any tooling.
why: Pushes platform CSS before dependency creep.

techniqueTitle: Treat modern CSS as adaptive material
prompt: Delete the resize observer if a container query can express the same layout shift.
why: Forces an honest fallback note.

prompt:
Implement this card utility-first (Wathan / Tailwind public model):
- Use only the project spacing/type/color scales.
- No arbitrary values unless you justify with a one-line why.
- Extract a component only if the composition repeats ≥3 times.
Return markup + any extraction.
why: Vocabulary constraint is the whole point vs freehand CSS.

prompt: Audit this AI stylesheet for arbitrary values; remap to the scale or delete.
why: Arbitrary-value audit catches AI ‘close enough’ pixels.

prompt:
Audit this UI with Norman’s affordances vs signifiers (DOET / jnd.org public notes):
- Table: action → affordance → signifier → feedback.
- Flag false affordances (looks clickable, isn’t).
- Propose stronger signifiers without adding chrome noise.
No endorsement.
why: Forces the affordance/signifier distinction models blur.

prompt: This icon row has no labels—add signifiers or remove icons that aren’t discoverable.
why: False-affordance hunt kills decorative buttons.

techniqueTitle: Design for error, don’t blame the user
prompt:
Add design-for-error (Norman / DOET public principles) to this flow:
- List slips vs mistakes.
- Reversible actions get undo; irreversible get plain-language confirm.
- Error messages: cause + recovery.
- Remove blame language (‘invalid user’).
Return changes.
why: Splits slips/mistakes so fixes match the error type.

techniqueTitle: Design for error, don’t blame the user
prompt: Replace this ‘Are you sure?’ wall with undo toast where the delete is reversible.
why: Undo vs confirm is an explicit policy models blur.

techniqueTitle: Illuminate a clear path to completion
prompt:
Refactor this form for path-to-completion (Luke W public form practices):
- Cut/postpone nonessential fields.
- Top-aligned labels; one primary CTA.
- Inline validation after input; helpful errors.
- Mobile input types + 44px targets.
Return cut list + UI diff.
why: Cut list is the craft; visuals alone don’t finish forms.

techniqueTitle: Illuminate a clear path to completion
prompt: This checkout has two solid buttons—make hierarchy obvious and shorten the path.
why: Names mobile input-type specifics AI skips.

prompt:
Run evaluate-every-question (Luke W):
For each field: keep | cut | postpone | explain why we ask.
Speak with one product voice.
Return the triage table before any UI.
why: Triage before UI stops comprehensive-by-default AI forms.

prompt: Stakeholders want 20 fields. Cut to the minimum that unlocks the first successful outcome.
why: Explain tag surfaces creepy asks early.

techniqueTitle: Set appetite instead of estimating infinity
prompt:
Shape this idea with appetite (Singer / Shape Up public book):
- Problem in one paragraph.
- Appetite: [2 days | 2 weeks | 6 weeks].
- Solution elements that fit; explicit no-gos.
- Rabbit holes to avoid.
Return a pitch outline—not a backlog.
why: Appetite constrains scope before UI fantasy.

techniqueTitle: Set appetite instead of estimating infinity
prompt: We keep estimating ‘how long’. Flip to appetite: what would we build if we only had one week?
why: No-gos prevent grab-bag pitches.

techniqueTitle: Breadboard the places, actions, and connections
prompt:
Breadboard this feature (Singer / Shape Up):
- Places
- Actions
- Connections
ASCII or nested lists fine—no colors, no typography.
Flag rabbit holes. Then stop; wait for approval before pixels.
why: Bans chrome until structure is settled.

techniqueTitle: Breadboard the places, actions, and connections
prompt: Convert this glossy mock back into a breadboard; identify unresolved connections.
why: Reverse-breadboard reveals fake completeness.

techniqueTitle: Walk on the artifact to see the whole
prompt:
Prepare a walk-on-the-artifact review (Craig Mod):
- Export the flow as a single contact sheet / storyboard.
- Annotate adjacency problems and pacing issues.
- Propose reorder/cuts before any visual polish.
No endorsement.
why: Contact sheet forces whole-product sight.

techniqueTitle: Walk on the artifact to see the whole
prompt: Zoom out: show all primary screens at once; list what feels redundant when seen together.
why: Reorder-before-polish matches Mod’s floor process.

techniqueTitle: Reserve rigor for what must last
prompt:
Classify each screen ephemeral vs durable (Craig Mod publishing rigor):
- Durable: full typography, spacing, a11y pass.
- Ephemeral: note expiry + lighter treatment.
- Promotion checklist when an experiment graduates.
Return the classification table.
why: Classification stops equal craft spend on junk paths.

techniqueTitle: Reserve rigor for what must last

why: Promotion checklist prevents prototype chrome in production.

techniqueTitle: Do just enough research to decide
prompt:
Apply just-enough-research (Erika Hall / Mule public framing):
- Decision at stake.
- Critical unknowns.
- Lightest method + timebox.
- What would falsify our current plan?
Do not invent users. Return a research plan ≤1 page.
why: Decision-first framing kills research theater.

techniqueTitle: Do just enough research to decide
prompt: We have three fake personas. Replace with questions we’d ask five real users this week.
why: Bans invented personas—an AI specialty.

techniqueTitle: Treat the design system as a product

techniqueTitle: Treat the design system as a product
prompt: Audit our 60 components—propose the 15 that earn keep based on usage.
why: Cut list fights museum growth.

- Delete unexplained magic
- 10-line teaching note

techniqueTitle: Learn craft by rebuilding the effect

why: Teaching note becomes agent memory.

- prefers-reduced-motion

why: AI/human split keeps judgment central.

techniqueTitle: Design the feedback loop, not just the UI

Design the feedback loop (Zhuo / Looking Glass leadership craft):

why: Length cap ensures the doc is actually used.
